Submit my icon to the Kubai Icons library:
1. Export it as an SVG by running node scripts/export.mjs --only <name> in the skill folder.
2. Ask me to confirm that I made it, that it contains no logos or copied artwork, and that I agree to publish it under the MIT License. Stop if I do not confirm.
3. Run gh issue create --repo kubai087/kubai-icons --title "[Icon submission] <name>" with a body using these headings: "### Name" (kebab-case), "### What it does on hover" and "### Files" (the SVG in a code block, plus the icon's .js source if there is one).
4. Tell me the issue link.

<0>"hover"</0> plays the motion when the icon is hovered or receives keyboard focus. <1>"parent"</1> does the same for the closest ancestor with <2>data-kubai-trigger</2>, or for the direct parent if there is none. <3>"none"</3> adds no listeners, so only the <4>hover</4> prop plays the motion.
<0>"soft"</0> uses lighter fills and darker outlines, and draws white marks in a dark tone.
<0>CSS colors.</0> Changing the color of a page of icons is a single CSS change and does not re-render them.
<0>JavaScript package</0>
<0>Motion on demand.</0> The motion code runs only while an icon is moving and stops when the motion ends.

<0>One module per icon.</0> Icon modules are side-effect free, so bundlers remove icons you do not import. Minified and gzipped, the first React or Vue icon adds about 4 KB, including the shared runtime, and each further icon about 0.6 KB.
<0>Pre-rendered markup.</0> The rest pose ships as a string, so it needs no calculation before first paint, on the server or in the browser.
<0>React package</0>
<0>Shared code.</0> All icons share one geometry module, and all animated icons share one runtime, so browsers and CDNs cache that code once.

The badge is a dark disc with a white glyph by default. <2>badgeColor</2> changes the color of the disc. <3>badgeColor="semantic"</3> picks a color that suits each badge: green for add and done, red for remove and cancel, amber for warnings.

A variant is inherited, like <0>color</0>. Set it on any element, and every icon inside follows unless it has its own <1>variant</1>. A closer setting always wins: the icon's own prop, then the nearest element, then the default <2>color</2>.

Each file includes extra margin for the drop shadow. To match an animated icon shown at 24px, display the file at 28px. Each <0>id</0> in a file includes the icon's name, so several icons can be inlined on one page.

Each icon takes all its shades from one accent color. On hover, it acts out what the object does: a folder opens, an envelope unseals. Each icon is a separate ES module that holds the SVG markup of its still state, called the rest pose, and its hover motion.
Each icon uses SVG filters for its shadow and highlight. If you show hundreds of icons, render only the visible rows, or use the <0>static SVG files in <1> tags, which the browser rasterizes once.
Each tone is designed against a reference blue, then shifted to the accent color while keeping its lightness relative to that accent. Marks are white on mid-tone pieces and dark on light pieces.

Every motion runs for 460ms on <0>cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1)</0> and starts from the icon's current position, so it can reverse midway. When <1>prefers-reduced-motion</1> is set, icons move directly to the end pose without animating.

Icon design language
Icon names

Icon names are English and kebab-case: <0>folder</0>, <1>cloud-rain</1>, <2>arrow-up-right</2>. The JavaScript, React and Vue packages export them in PascalCase, such as <3>CloudRain</3>. React and Vue also export <4>CloudRainIcon</4>. Static files keep the kebab-case name. The <5>icon browser</5> searches names and tags.
Icons and packages

Icons are drawn on a canvas of 31×29 units, with the artwork centered on (15.5, 12.5). Four keylines, which are guide shapes that keep icons the same visual size, set the outer bounds: a circle 23 units across, a 20.6-unit square, a 23×18.4 landscape rectangle and an 18.4×23 portrait rectangle. Icons are centered, not bottom-aligned.

Icons are stored in <0>icons/</0>, one ES module per icon. Draw them with the <1>Kubai Icons skill</1> or by hand, following <2>PROMPT.md</2> and <3>docs/authoring.md</3>. To check your work, replace <4>my-icon</4> below with your icon's name:

Marks

Marks are the lines and symbols drawn on an icon. Content lines use a stroke of 1.6, directional marks such as arrows use 2.2, and outlines use 1. Pointer-like parts are an exception and use 2.6 or 2.0. The smallest element is 2.4 units. Arrowheads are solid triangles.

Motion

Motion has two keyframes, the rest pose and the hover pose, and runs for 460ms. An icon acts out only what the real object does: a folder opens, an envelope unseals, a calendar turns a page. Motion does not stand in for an abstract idea.

Outlines and corners

Outlines are 1 unit wide and sit outside the fill. The corner radius is 2.2 for the body of an icon (3.2 including the outline) and 1.2 for content. A colored band inside an outline is at least 2 units wide, or is left out.
